contact.label: Your email
contact.help: The address you will sign in with when your access opens.

contact.label: What do you spend your days on?
contact.help: A sentence is plenty. It tells us what your brain will need to be good at.

questions.question: How do you want your connections set up?
questions.help: Your brain reaches sources like Slack and Google through small "connector apps" (the registered doorway a service uses to grant access). Either way your data, your database, and your brain stay yours: managed only hosts the doorway, never what passes through it. Honest scope today: managed makes Slack a single approval, and the remaining connectors keep the guided self-hosted steps until our hosted apps clear each service's review (Google's verification in particular takes a long time).

options.label: Managed, easy setup
options.hint: We host the connector apps. One approval replaces app creation where supported.

options.label: Self-hosted, full control
options.hint: You create each connector app yourself, in your own accounts. Everything runs in your name.

questions.question: What computer do you use day to day?
Do you have a computer that stays on ALL the time?
questions.help: This means a machine that is awake even when nobody is touching it, like a Mac mini or a desktop in a closet that never sleeps. Your everyday laptop does NOT count: it sleeps when the lid closes.

options.label: Yes, a desktop or Mac mini that never sleeps
No, just my laptop and phone

questions.question: Where should your brain run?
questions.help: Both answers are YOUR infrastructure; there is no "we host it for you" option, because we never hold your memory. The choice is whether it lives on hosting you rent or on a Mac you already own, and it changes which accounts you sign up for. Neither one can read your iMessages or Apple Notes yet.

options.label: In the cloud, on hosting in my name
options.hint: Your own Railway and Supabase accounts, about $20 a month. Reachable from your phone with every device of yours switched off. Most people pick this.

options.label: On my own always-on Mac
options.hint: No monthly hosting bill, and nothing leaves your house except what you connect. Needs a free Tailscale account to be reachable, and the Mac has to stay awake: when it sleeps, your brain is unreachable.

questions.question: Which AI assistants do you use?
questions.help: Your brain plugs into the AI apps you already talk to. Pick all that apply; the checklist shapes itself around them.

options.label: Yes, my team lives in it

Which note-taking apps do you use?

required.name: OpenAI
required.what: Turns your documents into searchable memory (the embeddings your brain searches over).
required.cost: Pay for what you use, needs a card, typically a few dollars a month for one person.

required.name: Anthropic
required.what: Claude is the mind your brain thinks with: it reads your email, writes your brief, files your to-dos.
required.cost: Pay for what you use, needs a card, typically a few dollars a month for one person.

required.name: Supabase
required.what: The database where your brain's memory lives, in a project only you own.
required.cost: Free tier is enough to start; a busy brain outgrows it to about $25 a month.

required.name: Railway
required.what: The always-on computer in the cloud where your brain runs, so it answers from your phone with every device of yours turned off.
required.cost: About $20 a month (Railway's Pro plan). Nothing is charged until your brain actually starts.

conditional.name: Google Cloud
conditional.what: The "connector app" that lets your brain read your own Google Drive and Gmail. Free to create; it is a registration, not a service you buy.
conditional.onlyIf: only if you use Google Drive or Gmail

conditional.name: Claude (Pro or Max)
conditional.what: The app you talk to your brain in, on your phone and desktop. Custom connectors need a paid Claude plan.
conditional.cost: From about $20 a month, paid to Anthropic separately from the API usage above.
conditional.onlyIf: only if you talk to your brain in Claude

conditional.name: Telegram
conditional.what: How your brain reaches YOU: the daily brief and nudges arrive as messages.
conditional.onlyIf: needed to finish, unless you take your brain's messages in Slack instead

conditional.name: Notion
conditional.what: Your Notion pages become part of your brain's memory.
conditional.cost: Whatever you already pay Notion; the connection itself is free.
conditional.onlyIf: only if you use Notion sync

conditional.name: Slack
conditional.what: Your brain reads the Slack conversations you can already see.
conditional.cost: Whatever your workspace already pays; the connection itself is free.
conditional.onlyIf: only if you use Slack memory

conditional.name: Plaid
conditional.what: Pulls your account balances in so your brain can answer money questions.
conditional.cost: Free in development mode for your own accounts.

conditional.name: WHOOP
conditional.what: Sleep and recovery numbers land in your brain alongside everything else.
conditional.cost: Whatever you already pay WHOOP; the developer access is free.
conditional.onlyIf: only if you use WHOOP health ingest

cloud.cost: About $20 a month for hosting, plus a few dollars a month of AI usage. Your database starts on Supabase's free tier and only costs anything (about $25 a month) if you outgrow it. No hardware to buy, and it answers your phone with every device of yours switched off.
cloud.ownership: Every account is in your name, every bill is yours, and so is the data. We never hold your accounts, your credentials, or your memory — you can cancel any of it without asking us.
notYet: Your texts (iMessage) and Apple Notes cannot flow into your brain yet, on either path. Choosing the Mac does not unlock them today; the piece that reads them is still being built.
